questions.title: Find First Non-Repeating Character in a String
questions.problem_statement: Write a function to find the first non-repeating character in a given string and return its index. If all characters repeat, return -1.
questions.hint: Use a frequency map or an integer array of size 256 to count occurrences in a first pass, then check the string sequentially.

questions.title: Check for Balanced Parentheses in an Expression
questions.problem_statement: Given a string containing parentheses '()', '{}', and '[]', determine if the input string is valid and balanced.
questions.hint: Push opening brackets onto a Stack. When a closing bracket is encountered, check if it matches the top element of the Stack.

questions.title: Java Interface vs Inheritance & Multiple Inheritance Workaround
questions.problem_statement: Why does Java not support multiple inheritance with classes? Explain how Java achieves multiple inheritance using interfaces and default methods.
questions.hint: Address the Diamond Problem where two parent classes define the same method signature.

questions.title: SQL GROUP BY & HAVING Clause Aggregation
questions.problem_statement: Write a SQL query to display department IDs and the total number of employees in each department, showing only departments that have more than 5 employees.
questions.hint: Use SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) FROM Employee GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5.

questions.title: DBMS ACID Properties & Transaction Consistency
questions.problem_statement: Explain the ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) properties of database management systems with a bank transfer example.
questions.hint: Atomicity ensures all-or-nothing execution; Durability ensures committed changes survive system crashes.

questions.title: Operating Systems Virtual Memory vs Physical RAM
questions.problem_statement: What is Virtual Memory in operating systems? Explain how Paging and the Memory Management Unit (MMU) map virtual addresses to physical RAM frames.
questions.hint: Virtual memory provides an illusion of a large contiguous memory space using secondary storage swap space.

questions.title: Computer Networks TCP vs UDP Protocols
questions.problem_statement: Differentiate between TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol). Mention real-world applications for each.
questions.hint: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable (web, email); UDP is connectionless and fast (video streaming, gaming).

questions.title: Profit and Loss Marked Price Discount
questions.problem_statement: An article is sold at a discount of 15% on its marked price of $200. If the seller still makes a profit of 10%, what was the cost price of the article?

questions.title: Ages Ratio & Linear Equation
questions.problem_statement: The present ratio of ages of A and B is 4:5. Six years hence, the ratio of their ages will become 5:6. What is the present age of A?

questions.title: Speed, Distance & Relative Velocity
questions.problem_statement: Two cars start from points X and Y (180 km apart) toward each other at speeds of 40 km/h and 50 km/h respectively. How long will it take for them to meet?
questions.hint: Relative speed when moving in opposite directions = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h. Time = Distance / Relative Speed = 180 / 90.

questions.title: Logical Reasoning Syllogism
questions.problem_statement: Statements: 'All software is code. Some code is open-source.' Conclusions: I. Some software is open-source. II. All code is software.
questions.hint: No direct intersection between software and open-source is guaranteed, and 'all software is code' does not imply 'all code is software'.

questions.title: Probability Cards Selection
questions.problem_statement: From a standard deck of 52 cards, two cards are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both cards drawn are Kings?

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.problem_statement: Tell me about yourself, your academic background, core technical skills, and key project experiences.
questions.hint: Deliver a concise elevator pitch covering degree specialization, programming skills, major project role, and career goals.

questions.title: Why Do You Want to Join Cognizant?
questions.problem_statement: Why do you want to join Cognizant (CTS) specifically?
questions.hint: Highlight Cognizant's industry leadership in digital transformation, cloud services, continuous learning platforms, and employee growth.

questions.title: Why Should We Hire You?
questions.problem_statement: Why should Cognizant hire you for a software engineering position?
questions.hint: Align your problem-solving capability, fast adaptability to new tech stacks, and team-player mindset with Cognizant's requirements.

questions.title: Explain Your Final-Year Project
questions.problem_statement: Explain your final-year academic project, architecture, and your individual contribution.
questions.hint: Detail the project objective, tech stack, your specific responsibilities, challenges overcome, and final achievements.

questions.title: Motivation to Work in IT
questions.problem_statement: What motivates you to pursue a long-term career in the IT industry?
questions.hint: Discuss passion for technology innovation, solving real-world business problems, and lifelong learning.

questions.title: Handling Pressure and Tight Deadlines
questions.problem_statement: How do you handle high pressure, tight project deadlines, and unexpected technical hurdles?
questions.hint: Emphasize task prioritization, calm breakdown of issues, communication with mentors, and systematic execution.

questions.title: Willingness to Relocate
questions.problem_statement: Are you willing to relocate to any Cognizant development center across India/globally?
questions.hint: Express clear willingness, enthusiasm for professional exposure, and flexibility.
